original_test_intent: Verify that an isolated RAID5 remains accessible during one-member hot removal, safely accepts bounded degraded operations, reintegrates the member through a complete rebuild, and preserves data/parity across five cycles per member.
original_method: Bind array UUID, RAID implementation, geometry and member serial/WWN-to-bay map; use a disposable corpus; remove one approved member; perform bounded degraded I/O; reinsert it; wait for full rebuild; verify corpus hashes, array metadata, member health and parity consistency before any next cycle.
manual_activity: Operator removes/reinserts the exact labeled RAID5 member only after array, serial/WWN, bay and single-fault readiness are verified.
required_inputs: Disposable non-production RAID5 array UUID and geometry
safety_requirements: Require optimal baseline and recent health evidence
Stop immediately on second fault, URE, timeout or parity error
Do not re-pull during rebuild or consistency check
Require full rebuild and parity verification
agent_execution_scope: Verify exclusions, health and optimal baseline
Hash full corpus and inspect all media health
Record each member/cycle and report without final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Enumeration, dmesg and RAID status are necessary but omit exact stack/geometry, data operations, rebuild completion, parity verification and second-fault gates.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each member and five cycles, prove optimal RAID5, pull the mapped member, validate degraded access with bounded approved I/O, reinsert it, complete rebuild, run parity consistency checks, then verify corpus hashes and all member health before continuing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RAID5, one-member removal, degraded copy/delete, reinsertion, visibility, MD5, all members, five cycles and 40/20-minute timing are preserved; targets and implementation are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a parity-array cycle ledger containing geometry, member event count, degraded write manifest, rebuild rate/ETA, parity-check result, URE counters and final hashes.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds RAID5-specific parity and second-fault evidence beyond generic array detection.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects incomplete rebuild, latent read error, parity inconsistency, wrong member and silent corruption after degraded writes.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RAID5 has no redundancy during a one-member degradation; full-stripe/reconstruction writes and latent errors materially increase data-loss risk.

project_override_considerations: Tool selection must match the actual software or hardware RAID stack. The private software-RAID script cannot be assumed valid for a controller-managed RAID5 or sufficient for parity validation.
expected_evidence: Per-cycle degraded events and I/O results
Final corpus hashes and array state
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets RAID5 one-member hot-plug and recovery. Missing topology and parity specifics are execution prerequisites.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An isolated array, topology, backup and rebuild procedure are finite inputs; unknown/unsafe targets or unresolved recovery after request would block execution.

review_improvement: Makes parity reconstruction and second-fault exposure explicit so a merely detected RAID5 cannot pass without complete, consistent recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike a mirror, degraded RAID5 reconstructs missing data from parity on every affected read and updates parity during writes, increasing load and exposure to latent errors. Therefore optimal baseline, strict single-fault control, full rebuild and parity verification are essential. Physical handling plus destructive I/O require package and confirmation.
